name: Burg Heinfels
kurzbeschreibung: The imposing hilltop fortress Burg Heinfels in East Tyrol's Hochpustertal reigns as the Queen of the Pustertal with panoramic views and museum exhibitions.
beschreibung:
Overview

The mighty and far-visible Heinfels Castle (Burg Heinfels) perches atop a precipitous rocky spur high above the confluence of the Drau and Villgraten rivers in East Tyrol's high Pustertal valley. Dominating the alpine landscape for centuries, this formidable medieval stronghold is affectionately known throughout the Alpine region as the «Queen of the Pustertal». The monumental fortress was founded in the early 13th century by the Counts of Görz as a strategic border bastion and expanded over subsequent centuries into an extensive fortification. Following years of meticulous historical renovation, this storied cultural heritage site radiates with renewed splendor, captivating history enthusiasts, families, and alpine travelers from across the globe.

Route & Requirements

The multifaceted tour through the museum complex illuminates its architectural evolution from a Romanesque core castle to early modern artillery bastions. Visitors explore the imposing West Wing, the historic Knights' Hall, the late Gothic Saint Lawrence Chapel, and the formidable keep. A state-of-the-art permanent exhibition brings history alive with interactive media stations, models, and archaeological finds, showcasing life at the court of the Counts of Görz, medieval jurisdiction, and regional conflicts. From the wooden battlements and the observation deck on the main tower, a breathtaking 360-degree panorama unfolds across the Sexten Dolomites, Villgraten Valley, and the jagged Lienz Dolomites. Sturdy walking shoes are recommended for the historic stone steps.

Visit & Arrival

Heinfels Castle welcomes visitors from May to October: Tuesday through Sunday from 10:00 to 17:00, and daily during the peak summer months of July and August. Visits are possible individually with multilingual audio guides or via guided tours. Admission fees: adults approx. €11.00, children €6.00; family passes available. Arrival by rail: take the ÖBB train along the Drau Valley line to Sillian station; from there, a signposted panoramic walking trail reaches the fortress in about twenty minutes. By car: via the B100 Drautal federal road directly to Heinfels, where spacious parking is available at the base of the castle hill.

Tips

Take advantage of the scenic footpath up the historic castle ramp for memorable photographic angles of the battlements. A major architectural jewel at the foot of the castle hill is the protected wooden Punbrücke bridge from 1781, the longest covered wooden bridge in East Tyrol spanning the rushing Drau River. After touring the fortress, enjoy a stroll through neighboring Sillian or relax at the castle café's scenic terrace.
preis: Adults approx. €11.00, concessions €8.50, children €6.00 (family tickets available)
